name: Strontium carbonate
description: Strontium carbonate (CAS 1633-05-2 ), also identified under the colorant index reference CI 77837, is an inorganic mineral salt used across ceramics, electronics, and specialty chemical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a strontium source in high-temperature processing and as a stabilizing or buffering agent in formulated systems. In the electronics industry, it is a key raw material for producing cathode ray tube glass. Ferrite components also utilize this material, where controlled strontium content directly affects dielectric performance. Coatings formulators incorporate it as a corrosion-inhibiting pigment in anti-rust primers. In these applications, it neutralizes acidic byproducts and passivates metal substrates. In plastics and polymer compounding, it acts as a heat and light stabilizer, extending service life in PVC and related systems. Pharmaceutical and specialty chemical producers also use it as a catalyst precursor and pH-buffering agent. It is essential in various synthesis and processing applications requiring high chemical stability. Strontium carbonate is supplied as a fine white powder in technical and high-purity grades. Particle size distribution varies by grade, with finer cuts available for electronic and coating applications. Surface coverage and reactivity are critical factors in these specialized sectors.
